cards.title: BP myths live in every family
cards.body: Heard at weddings, repeated in WhatsApp groups. Here are five common ones, and the one rule that beats them all.

cards.title: Myth: BP is normal now, so stop
cards.body: Normal readings often mean the medicine is doing its job. Never stop or reduce a BP medicine without talking to the doctor.

cards.title: Myth: I feel fine, so BP's fine
cards.body: High BP often has no symptoms at all. The only way to know is to check it, as often as the doctor suggests.

cards.title: Myth: once started, stuck forever
cards.body: Some people need long-term treatment, some see changes over time. That's the doctor's call, based on readings, not fear.

cards.title: Myth: extra tablet on a high day
cards.body: Don't add doses on your own when a reading is high. Note it and call the doctor. High BP with chest pain, confusion or one-sided weakness: call 112.

cards.title: Myth: home remedies can replace it
cards.body: Less salt, walking and good sleep do help. Whether they're enough instead of medicine is for the doctor to decide.

cards.title: One rule beats every myth
cards.body: Any change to BP medicine goes through the doctor first. Keep readings handy so that conversation is actually useful.

takeaway: Don't stop, skip or add BP medicines on your own. Track readings and take any change to the doctor.
share: Send this to the Mama who stops his BP tablet every time he feels fine.
